369 :          \s+%s=['"]?%s['"]?
370 :          (?:\s+[a-zA-Z0-9:._-]+(?:=[a-zA-Z0-9:._-]*|="[^"]*"|='[^']*'))*?
371 :         \s*>
372 :         (?P<content>.*?)
373 :         </\1>

381 :

Conclusion: The test `test_get_element_by_attribute` checks whether the function `get_elements_by_attribute` correctly retrieves the content of the tag with the specified attribute in the passed HTML document. However, the test failure indicates that this is not the case for the itemprop attribute. Following the execution path, we find that while the regular expression used to match tags has been escaped appropriately (`value = re.escape(value)`), it does not correctly handle the case where the value contains special characters like `"` or `'`. Consequently, when matching `
foo
` with attribute `itemprop` and value `author`, the regular expression fails to match due to the presence of `"`. This leads to an empty list being returned by `get_elements_by_attribute`, causing it to return `None` in `get_element_by_attribute`, which ultimately causes the AssertionError. Methods to be fixed: - youtube_dl.utils.get_elements_by_attribute(attribute, value, html, escape_value=True)
